summary: Rabbi Hidary explores the significance of the Bet HaMikdash beyond its role in sacrifices, focusing on its architecture, its function as a center for national comfort, and its role as the seat of the Sanhedrin. He explains how the daily rituals of the Kohanim were a reenactment of the themes in Shir HaShirim, representing the intimate relationship between Hashem and the Jewish people. Finally, he discusses how we can maintain these pillars of Torah, Abodah, and Gemilut Hasadim in our own lives to prepare for the rebuilding of the Bet HaMikdash.
questions: Why do we still mourn the Bet HaMikdash when we have a thriving state of Israel?
What is the connection between the daily rituals of the Kohanim and Shir HaShirim?
How did the Bet HaMikdash serve as a place of national comfort for individuals in distress?
What role did the Sanhedrin play in preventing division among the Jewish people?
How can we rebuild the pillars of the world today in the absence of the Bet HaMikdash?
